methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Nyobolt, a Series B Climate & Energy company founded by Sai Shivareddy and Clare Grey, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public peer (LNZA). The target has raised $100M+ to date. Three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) form the primary comparison set.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, anchored to the $100M total raised proxy, yielding $190M. Peer-median analysis across the three comparable companies produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The peer set reflects material heterogeneity in valuation outcomes within the same sector and stage band.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a low estimate of $162M, a median of $595M, and a high of $1.1B. The wide spread—from $162M to $1.1B—reflects tension between the conservative stage-progression framework and the higher peer-median benchmark. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three peer valuations, variation in technology maturity and capital efficiency within the peer set, and the degree to which $100M raised is a reliable anchor for pre-money valuation. The median estimate of $595M serves as a central reference, though the range bounds material estimation risk.
